# EnhancedArticleWithVersions vs. `prod--epp.elifesciences.org/api/preprints/{id}` — discrepancy report

Scanned all **9340** entries from `GET /api/preprints` against `GET /api/preprints/{id}`, comparing the response shape to the `EnhancedArticleWithVersions` type (`src/types/enhanced-article.ts` and referenced types). **8903** returned 200 and were checked; **437** returned 404 (see [404s](#404s---ids-present-in-the-list-but-missing-from-the-detail-endpoint) below).

> **Note on coverage:** the original checker validated one level of shape for `Reference` but didn't recurse into its nested `isPartOf` (`Publication`), `publisher`, `comments[]`, or `identifiers[]` objects. A follow-up pass added that recursion and re-scanned all 8907 200-responses (counts shifted slightly — 4 IDs flipped between 200/404 between runs). It surfaced one real issue, #11 below; the `publisher`/`comments`/`identifiers` shapes turned out to match the types fine.
>
> **Second follow-up pass:** to close out any remaining blind spots, the checker was rewritten as a single generic, declarative, table-driven validator — every nested object/array/union in the full type surface (`EnhancedArticleWithVersions` → `EnhancedArticle` → `ProcessedArticle` → `Content` union → `Author`/`Institution`/`Reference`/`Publication`/`Publisher`/`Comment` → `PeerReview`/`Evaluation`/`Participant` → `Metrics`/`RelatedContent` → the `VersionSummary` union) is walked automatically from one schema table, rather than via separate hand-written checks per type, so a recursion can no longer be silently forgotten the way it was for `isPartOf`. Re-scanned all 8908 200-responses; found two more real issues (#12, #13 below). Everything else it checked — literal/enum values, required-field presence, unknown keys, and basic type correctness (string/number/boolean/array) — matched the declared types at every remaining depth, including `Author`/`Reference` `identifiers[]`, `Publisher`, `Comment`, ISO-datetime format on every date field, and every `Content` node's field set.

## Summary

| # | Discrepancy | Records affected | % of 200s |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ProcessedArticle.headings` (required) never present in the API | 8903 | 100.0% |
| 2 | `versions[k]` (preprint-stage) carries extra `EnhancedArticle`-level fields not in any `VersionSummary` variant | 8903 | 100.0% |
| 3 | `versions[k]` (VOR-stage) carries extra `url` not in any variant | 7168 | 80.5% |
| 4 | `ImageObjectContent` missing `mediaType` | 8896 | 99.9% |
| 5 | `Institution` (author affiliations) carries extra `type` | 8902 | 100.0% |
| 6 | `LinkContent` carries extra `id`/`title` | 4829 | 54.2% |
| 7 | `ClaimContent` carries extra `id` | 48 | 0.5% |
| 8 | Undeclared `Content` node type `QuoteBlock` | 2 | 0.0% |
| 9 | Undeclared `Content` node type `Note` | 5 | 0.1% |
| 10 | `Author` carries extra `honorificPrefix` | 9 | 0.1% |
| 11 | `Reference.isPartOf.type` has values outside the declared union (`CreativeWork`, `PublicationIssue`) — *found in a follow-up pass, see note below* | 2687 | 30.2% |
| 12 | `HeadingContent.id` (required) frequently missing (captions, some back-matter sections) — *found in a second follow-up pass* | 8825 | 99.1% |
| 13 | `Publication.issueNumber` sometimes a string, not just a number | 204 | 2.3% |

## 1. `ProcessedArticle.headings` (required) never present in the API

`headings: Heading[]` is declared as a required field on `ProcessedArticle` (`src/types/enhanced-article.ts`), but it never appears in the raw API response for `article.article`. It's computed client-side via `contentToHeadings(content)` in `src/pages/reviewed-preprints/[...path].page.tsx:63`, not returned by the API. Affects effectively all 200 responses.

**8903** of 8903 records affected.

## 2. `versions[k]` (preprint-stage entries) carry extra `EnhancedArticle`-level fields

For preprint-stage version entries, the API includes `eLocationId`, `license`, `peerReview`, `publishedYear`, `relatedContent`, `subjects`, `volume` — none of which are declared on `PreprintVersionSummary` (`src/fetch-data/version-summary/preprint-version-summary.ts`). In practice these entries look like almost the full `EnhancedArticle` shape minus the nested `article: ProcessedArticle`. Affects effectively all 200 responses (every article has at least one preprint-stage version entry).

Additional detail from a deeper recursive pass: that embedded `peerReview` blob is itself not even a complete `PeerReview` — in every one of these entries it's missing the (declared-required) `reviews` array, containing only `evaluationSummary`. Since the field shouldn't be here at all per the type, this doesn't change the affected-ID list, just underlines that nothing downstream should rely on its shape.

**8903** of 8903 records affected.

## 11. `Reference.isPartOf.type` (`Publication.type`) has values outside the declared union

## 12. `HeadingContent.id` (required) is frequently missing

**Added in a second follow-up pass** — a fully generic, table-driven re-implementation of the checker (recursing into literally every declared nested object/array/union in the type surface, replacing the earlier hand-written per-type checks) found this. `HeadingContent` (`src/content/content.ts`) declares `id: string` as required. In practice:
- Heading nodes used as a figure/table caption's title line (nested under `caption`) almost never carry an `id` — there's no anchor to link to.
- Heading nodes for certain back-matter sections in the main content flow (e.g. "Acknowledgements") sometimes lack one too, even though most section headings (e.g. "Introduction", given `id: "s1"`) do have one.

**8825** of 8908 records affected (99.1%).

## 13. `Publication.issueNumber` is sometimes a string, not just a number

`issueNumber?: number` (`src/types/reference.ts`) — but real data has string values in this field. Sampled 31 real instances directly (independent spot-check, not just the scan output): about two-thirds are plain digit strings (e.g. `"13"`, `"87"`) that just happen to be typed as `string` rather than `number`, and the rest are genuinely non-numeric — article-number/e-location-style identifiers (`"e2111696118"`, `"E24010041"`), ISSN-like codes (`"S0197458022002019"`), MeSH-style IDs (`"D006142"`), and free-text values (`"6 Pt 1"`, `"November"`). `volumeNumber` on the same type is already `number | string`; `issueNumber` looks like it should be too — though note a `number | string` union still won't cover the free-text cases.

**204** of 8908 records affected.

## 404s — IDs present in the list but missing from the detail endpoint

**437** of 9340 IDs from `GET /api/preprints` returned `404 {"result":false,"message":"no result found for: (...)"}` when fetched individually via `GET /api/preprints/{id}`.

**Retried all 437 individually** (separate pass, same day): all 437 still return the identical 404. This is not transient. **436 of 437** are the highest version number listed for their `msid` (e.g. `85111v3` when `85111v1`/`v2` exist and return 200) — i.e. these are the VOR/published-stage version, which per the `versions[k]` findings above is only ever represented as a lightweight stub (`id`, `msid`, `doi`, `url`, `versionIdentifier`, `published`) and is never independently fetchable through this endpoint. One exception, `msid 108673`, where **both** `v3` and `v4` 404 (its last two listed versions are both inaccessible, not just the latest) — a minor outlier worth a manual look if pursued further.

Practical implication for a fetcher/validator built on this API: treat a 404 on `/api/preprints/{id}` as expected for an entry's final/VOR version, not as an error condition.
